channel.title: The Seax: Essex news, sport and life
channel.description: The latest Essex news, sport and life, updated through the day.

image.title: The Seax: Essex news, sport and life

item.title: A130 southbound shut all weekend between Howe Green and the Rayleigh Spur for maintenance
item.description: Drivers heading south from Chelmsford towards Basildon and Southend face a signed diversion via the A12 and A127 until early on Monday.

item.title: Thurrock's baby death rate is 37% above the national average, new health strategy warns
item.description: A draft Health and Wellbeing Strategy for 2027 to 2030 puts pregnancy and the early years at the centre of plans to give Thurrock babies a healthier start.

item.title: Met chief's call for just eight to ten forces sharpens fight over Essex Police's future
item.description: Sir Mark Rowley says the 43 forces in England and Wales should shrink to as few as eight, as Essex commissioner Roger Hirst insists the county wants to keep its own force.

item.title: Leigh Ward by-election called for Thursday 10 December
item.description: Nominations close at 4pm on 13 November; residents must register by 24 November and apply for a postal vote by 5pm on 25 November.

item.title: Plans emerge for 1GW solar and battery energy park on the Dengie Peninsula
item.description: Developer Low Carbon has started the national planning process for a scheme it says could power 250,000 homes, and Maldon District Council has until 24 November to say what studies it needs.

item.title: New website launched for 7,750-home Tendring Colchester Borders Garden Community
item.description: Three councils have opened a single online hub for the planned new town east of Colchester, with a decision on its planning application expected in summer 2027.

item.title: Essex County Council asks residents to help close a £170m gap in one of its toughest budgets this century
item.description: The county council has opened a month-long consultation on its 2027/28 budget, saying government funding changes will cost it more than £50m a year.

item.title: Rochford leader urges ministers to lift Local Plan hold or risk a consultation over Christmas
item.description: Rochford District Council says it cannot start the final public consultation on its Local Plan until the Government lifts a holding direction imposed on 2 October.

item.title: Colchester's parks and green spaces brought back under council-owned Amphora
item.description: About 40 grounds staff have moved from contractor Idverde to the council's own company, which now looks after almost 13,000 assets across 870 hectares.

item.title: New shop could open inside Southend's Fossetts Way Waitrose after store's makeover
item.description: Plans lodged with Southend council would carve a separate retail unit out of the refurbished supermarket off Eastern Avenue, though no tenant has been named.

item.title: Young Chelmsford writers to voice Cinderella's pre-show announcements
item.description: Three children aged 6 to 11 won Chelmsford Theatre's Voice of Panto competition, which drew a record number of entries this year.

item.title: Southend opens final consultation on Local Plan it was ordered to publish by ministers
item.description: Residents have until 21 December to comment on the draft blueprint for homes, jobs and infrastructure, which the city council published only after the housing minister intervened.

item.title: Hundreds run through Harlow Town Park for Let's Lift the Curfew women's safety event
item.description: Harlow Running and Tri-Club led an evening run backing the national campaign for women to exercise outdoors without changing their routines over safety fears.

item.title: Southend in Action week to showcase council teams from 9 to 13 November
item.description: The council will share videos and features on regeneration, community safety, business support, heritage and more, using the hashtag #SouthendInAction.

item.title: Disqualified drink-driver jailed after three-vehicle crash on London Road, Harlow
item.description: Nison Rajeswaren, 23, admitted drink-driving, driving while banned and having no insurance, and will spend a total of 31 weeks behind bars.

item.title: Abberton Reservoir exhibition marks what would have been writer Ronald Blythe's birthday
item.description: Essex Wildlife Trust has opened a new exhibition at its Abberton Reservoir centre honouring the writer Ronald Blythe.

item.title: Basildon councillors refuse 910-home Foots Farm scheme near Billericay's Sun Corner
item.description: The planning committee turned down the green belt application off Southend Road, but the developers' appeal is already heading to a public inquiry next May.

item.title: More than 50,000 still waiting at Southend Hospital as trust backlog falls by 14,000
item.description: Hospital chief executive Fiona Ryan told councillors there is still a long way to go, although waiting lists across the Mid and South Essex trust are starting to come down.

item.title: Former Essex maths teacher given further jail term for grooming and abusing girls
item.description: Syed Ahmed, 38, who posed online as a teenage boy, was sentenced at Southwark Crown Court after a second trial, having already been jailed in 2025.

item.title: Harlow man admits cocaine supply and £82,000 criminal property charge
item.description: Jy Ward, 38, of Little Grove Field, pleaded guilty at Chelmsford Magistrates' Court and will be sentenced at Basildon Crown Court on 27 November.

item.title: Essex, Southend and Thurrock councils start work on 25-year plan for where homes, jobs and roads will go
item.description: The three upper-tier councils are preparing a Spatial Development Strategy for Greater Essex, a long-range blueprint that will steer growth while leaving individual sites to local plans.

item.title: Braintree district homes can put glass out at the kerb after £12m recycling plant upgrade
item.description: A rebuilt Biffa sorting plant near Ipswich, part-funded by Braintree District Council, can now handle glass bottles and jars from the district's new two-bin system.

item.title: Grays-raised Russell Brand faces sentencing on Monday after jury convicts him of rape and three sexual assaults
item.description: A jury at Southwark Crown Court convicted the Thurrock-born actor of offences against four women between 2004 and 2009. He will be sentenced on Monday.

item.title: Police hunt two cars after motorcyclist knocked off in suspected Chelmsford hit-and-run
item.description: Officers want footage of two cars said to have been driven erratically before they hit a motorbike at the Melbourne Avenue and Chignal Road junction and drove off.

item.title: Grays Athletic hand Lewis Clark the player-manager's job as club seeks a fresh start
item.description: The supporter-owned Isthmian North club has named a new three-man management team after a difficult spell.

item.title: Campaigners say Google turned away 54,000-name petition against Purfleet data centre on Arena Essex wildlife site
item.description: Buglife and Essex Wildlife Trust took their objections to Google's London headquarters over plans for four data centre buildings on the former raceway near Purfleet.

item.title: Planning inquiry opens into 480-home 'Stanhanger' appeal on Green Belt between Stansted and Birchanger
item.description: Developer City and Country is appealing Uttlesford's refusal of two Green Belt schemes, with more than 40 residents at the opening day and a decision due after closing submissions on 27 November.

item.title: Harlow councillors approve rebuild of Sir Frederick Gibberd College after structural problems
item.description: Two new three-storey buildings for the secondary school and sixth form will replace the Tendring Road site's existing blocks, though completion may be years away.

item.title: New 24-hour NHS crisis text line opens for people in Essex struggling with their mental health
item.description: Texting SOS to 80899, or messaging on WhatsApp or webchat, now reaches trained health and care professionals at any time of day, with no minimum age.

item.title: Maldon Mud Race sponsor gives Basildon Hospital two Xbox gaming trolleys for young patients
item.description: A £3,060 gift from JR Revell Ltd pays for portable consoles that can be wheeled to children's and teenagers' bedsides.

item.title: No Christmas panto in Brentwood this year as theatre turns to Dickens and children's musicals
item.description: Neither Brentwood Theatre nor the Brentwood Centre lists a 2026 pantomime, leaving families to look to Basildon or Chelmsford for a traditional show.

item.title: Tendring police take 116 illegal e-scooters and e-bikes off the streets in three months
item.description: Officers say the latest sweep in Clacton seized 14 more machines and five uninsured cars, and led to two arrests.

item.title: Essex members given until Monday to renew at old price as Division One place is finally secured
item.description: With Leicestershire's appeal lost and top-flight status confirmed for 2027, Essex have held back their membership price rise so 2026 members can renew at the current rate until 9 November.

item.title: Maldon District groups can bid for Livewell health grants of up to £2,000
item.description: Voluntary groups, schools and social enterprises can apply for new projects tackling inactivity, isolation or mental health before 14 December.

item.title: Volunteers wanted for Tesco winter food collection on 26 to 28 November
item.description: Volunteers are sought for three-hour shifts at collection points in large Tesco stores, supporting Trussell food banks and the Felix charity network.

item.title: Graham Gooch presents Rochford sports awards as Heidi Nevin named Sports Personality of the Year
item.description: Athletes, coaches, volunteers and clubs from across the district were honoured at The Mill in Rayleigh.

item.title: Harlow's ECCO launches Green Lottery with first £150 draw this Friday
item.description: The environmental charity's new fortnightly lottery will raise money for local green, community and anti-poverty projects.

item.title: Police helicopter sent to Dengie marshes after reports of hare coursing
item.description: Essex Police's Rural Engagement Team, backed by the force helicopter, seized four dogs and four vehicles on the Dengie marshes, and five men were reported for hare coursing.

item.title: Great Baddow's Iron Age gold hoard goes into classrooms in new Museum of Chelmsford history kit
item.description: Primary schools can now hire a hands-on box built around the 935 gold coins found in Great Baddow in 2020, designed with help from local pupils.

item.title: Braintree Town Hall a finalist in the Essex Wedding Awards historic venues category
item.description: The 1920s town hall, given to Braintree by William Julien Courtauld, will learn its fate at a ceremony at Chelmsford Racecourse on 19 November.

item.title: HAVENS Hospices opens Light up a Life dedications for Christmas
item.description: Supporters can dedicate a light on the hospices' Christmas trees in memory of a loved one by Sunday 15 November.

item.title: Harlow Gymnastics Club shortlisted for Active Essex Sports Club of the Year and asks for votes
item.description: Public voting in the Active Essex Activity Awards 2026 closes at midnight on Sunday 8 November.

item.title: Free slippers and falls advice for older people at Rainbow Services' Ageing Well drop-in in Harlow
item.description: Around 25 stallholders, speakers and seated exercise sessions feature at a free morning event aimed at cutting falls among Harlow's older residents.

item.title: Harlow man, 37, charged with stalking a woman and damaging her letterbox
item.description: Police say the alleged campaign of unwanted calls, voicemails and visits ran for more than three weeks over the summer.

item.title: £25,000 gift transforms end-of-life rooms at Broomfield Hospital
item.description: Friends at Broomfield Hospital, backed by Chelmsford Round Table, funded five refurbished rooms through the hospitals charity's Dandelion Appeal.

item.title: Harlow Rugby Club hold off Wanstead fightback for fifth win in a row
item.description: A 31-14 half-time lead at Latton Park was almost wiped out as Harlow finished with 13 men, but Liam Batty's late penalty settled it.

item.title: Healthwatch Southend welcomes Government decision to keep patient watchdogs
item.description: Ministers have dropped plans to abolish Healthwatch England and local Healthwatch bodies, and say they will strengthen them instead.

item.title: Essex Police checked 200 lorries in national vehicle crime crackdown
item.description: Officers stopped 72 vehicles in a three-day push during Operation Alliances, which recovered more than 300 stolen vehicles across 32 forces.

item.title: Saffron Walden war memorial will not get a deep clean, town council says
item.description: The council says weathering on the Grade I listed memorial is normal and heavy cleaning could damage the stone.

item.title: £2,500 grant for Dovercourt's Christmas lights switch-on night
item.description: Harwich Town Council has backed the Harwich and Dovercourt Partnership's switch-on evening on Saturday 28 November.

item.title: Overnight clean-up after latest fly-tip on rural lane between Tilbury and West Tilbury
item.description: Thurrock Council's environmental services team cleared the dumped waste overnight after it was reported on Monday evening.

item.title: More than 75,000 handmade poppies on show for Chelmsford's Remembrance events
item.description: Chelmsford CVS says more than 75,000 knitted and crocheted poppies made by local people have been displayed at Remembrance events across the city.

item.title: Saffron Walden mayor invites young artists to design the town's Christmas e-card
item.description: The Town Council has launched a design competition for young people to create its Christmas e-card.

item.title: 45 free prostate cancer blood tests on offer at Harlow Town FC on 14 November
item.description: CHAPS Charity is running PSA tests for men aged 40 to 80 at Elizabeth Way from 11am to 3pm, by appointment only.

item.title: Police want to identify man after report of outraging public decency in Epping store
item.description: Officers have released an image of a man they want to speak to over an incident in a High Street shop at about 1pm on Friday 25 September.

item.title: Harlow Cycling Club honours Vin Denson, first Briton to win a Giro d'Italia stage
item.description: The club's honorary member, who rode the Tour de France alongside Jacques Anquetil and Tom Simpson, has died aged 90.

item.title: Racing returns to Chelmsford City, but Ladbrokes and Coral refuse to take bets
item.description: The Great Leighs track staged its first meeting since March under new operator Arc, with a betting row hanging over the comeback.

item.title: Henry Nowak's killer has minimum term raised to 25 years as appeal judges rule 21 years was unduly lenient
item.description: The Lady Chief Justice's panel found Vickrum Digwa's original sentence did not reflect the seriousness of the Chafford Hundred student's murder, and threw out his own bid to have it cut.

item.title: Walton's empty former fire station to be sold for computer repair business
item.description: Tendring District Council has agreed to sell the Mill Lane building, closed since 2017, to a local resident who plans to refurbish it.

item.title: Essex Police wins £30,000 to test how its drink and drug-drive crackdown deters offenders
item.description: The Road Safety Trust is funding a 12-month study of Operation Limit, the force's drink and drug-driving enforcement campaign.
